components.cost_effect: One projection per round; its internal computational cost is not treated as free.
components.goal: Return the next state after the gradient step to F and control its distance from a fixed comparator.
components.key_estimate: For u∈F, ||x_{t+1}−u||₂²≤||x_t−u||₂²−2η_t⟨g_t,x_t−u⟩+η_t²G²; the one-step relation in the source's Proof of Theorem 1.
components.name: Euclidean projection
components.requires: Nonempty closed convex F and exact Euclidean projection; g_t exact.
transfer_checks: Approximate projection or a noisy gradient requires a separate error analysis.
The Euclidean squared-distance estimate here cannot be reused directly for another geometry.

limitations.statement: Requires known F, feasible initialization, exact gradients, and exact projections; provides no guarantee on the internal efficiency of projection.
The record gives only a static regret upper bound for the selected Algorithm; it does not claim an unrestricted Oracle Complexity lower bound, dynamic regret, or an offline optimization rate.

performance_links.scope_note: Static regret, exact gradient/projection, η_t=t^(-1/2); no parameter rescaling.

variants.cost: Under complete execution of each round, there is one gradient computation and one exact Euclidean projection per round, for T calls of each type. Internal projection time/Oracle cost is counted separately, and the source gives no general complexity upper bound for it; the cost of obtaining an initial feasible point is also unbounded in the source. For a finite horizon requiring only the first T decisions, the final update may be omitted; T calls correspond to the complete-execution convention.
variants.name: Greedy Projection with η_t=t^(-1/2)
variants.output: Output a feasible decision x_t each round; regret evaluates x_1,...,x_T. x_{T+1} is the state after the final update, not an offline optimizer claimed by this record; no averaged-output guarantee is introduced.
public_inputs: Known nonempty closed bounded convex F⊆R^n
Exact Euclidean projection procedure for every y∈R^n
Gradient computation procedure after c_t is revealed
variants.query_and_update: Round t first outputs/selects x_t∈F; then receives c_t, computes g_t=∇c_t(x_t), and sets y_{t+1}=x_t−η_t g_t, x_{t+1}=P_F(y_{t+1}). Future costs are not queried in advance.
variants.requirements: Each round's c_t:F→R is convex and differentiable; the finite uniform bound ||∇c_t(x)||₂≤G holds for every t,x∈F. Exact gradients and P_F(y)=argmin_{x∈F}||x−y||₂ can be computed.
variants.state_and_initialization: Choose any x_1∈F; maintain the current feasible vector x_t and round index t=1,2,... .
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Use η_t=t^(-1/2), without prior knowledge of horizon T, D, or G. Run continuously; for a finite horizon T, take the first T rounds. Algorithm 1 originally allows any positive learning-rate sequence; the performance recorded here covers only this selected schedule.

use_restrictions: Independent Reviewer acceptance and publication not asserted.
Operation counts describe the explicit loop; projection runtime remains separately charged and unspecified.

links.note: Limited to η_t=t^(-1/2) and the complete assumptions of Theorem 1; revision is bound by this batch's prepare step.

source_refs.locator: PDF page 2 Definition 4; page 3 assumptions 1–7 and Algorithm 1; pages 3–4 Theorem 1 and Proof

summary: On a known convex feasible set, compute an exact gradient after each round's decision, then perform an exact Euclidean projection; the selected step size is t^(-1/2).
title: Online Gradient Descent / Greedy Projection
use_when: Establish a static regret guarantee against the best fixed feasible comparator for any convex cost sequence, with exact gradients and projections available.
